name: Seoul style
status: draft for stage 1 (2026-11-23): values match seoul/index.html; the spec, prompt and generated files come in stage 2
touchpoints: how Seoul shows a number to someone on the move: the station name signs on the platform wall (a band in the line colour along the wall, a white pill with a thick line-colour edge in the middle, the previous station on the ◀ side and the next on the ▶ side, thin bands for transfer lines), the subway map (octolinear, Line 2 drawn as a circle, white ticks for stations, traffic-light capsules for transfers, station numbers), the single-line diagram over the train doors, the bus information terminals at the stops (a black screen, the buses arriving soonest first and big, route numbers in their bus colours: trunk blue, branch green, express red, the 'arriving soon' words in yellow, crowding as plenty of seats · normal · crowded, other buses in a row of number and minutes, the stop number like 02-118), the city's crowding scale (light up to 80%, normal 80–130%, caution 130–150%, crowded 150% and over) and the crowding charts Seoul Metro publishes (bars in the line colour, the value over each bar, a dashed 150% line with a yellow tag)

devices.station-sign: KPI row: each KPI is a station sign. The label above; a 36px band in the line colour (all lines: #363743 with three 2px stripes in the line colours under it, like a transfer station's sign); a 62px white pill with a 3px edge in the band colour holds this week's value (38px/700 tabular, unit 18px); on the band, white, last week on the left (◀ value, 'last week' under it) and the plan, target or limit on the right (value ▶, the word under it). Under the sign one change, coloured by whether it is good: ▼1.0% under plan, ▲18 pts over limit. Peak crowding on all lines puts the line's number circle in the pill. Under 330px the pill is 56px and the value 32px; under 262px the side values move under the band on two lines
devices.line-map: Figure 1: a fictional network on an octolinear map (Line 2 a circle, Line 1 north–south, Line 3 west–east bending 45° at both ends). Each segment's width is its morning-peak crowding in the city's four steps (3 · 5.5 · 8.5 · 12.5px at full size: under 80, 80–130, 130–150, 150 and over), drawn from its busier direction. Stations are white ticks across the line; transfers are white capsules with a 1.5px ink edge and a dot per line. Segments at 150% and over carry a #ffd23f tag with the value (Line 2 inside the circle, Line 1 to the right, Line 3 above). Names only for transfers, the ends of the selected lines and the ends of segments over 150%, with a white halo. The selected line keeps its colour; the others turn #d3d6db
devices.single-line: Figure 3: the single-line diagram of the selected line (all lines: the most crowded one), stations top to bottom on a 6px strip in the line colour with white ticks and transfer capsules, the station number (10.5px muted, tabular) before each name. Both directions back to back from the strip: toward the end of the line on the right, back on the left, a bar per segment between its two stations. Bars grey #b3b7bd; only bars at 150% and over in the line colour. A #7a4a1e dashed 150% line on each side with a #ffd23f '150%' tag at its top (Seoul Metro's crowding chart). Values on bars at 150% and over and on each side's busiest bar
devices.bus-board: Figure 2: the one black surface (#0d0d0d, 12px corners). A header line (board name · Longest gap). The two most urgent routes in big tiles: a type letter square (B · G · R in its bus colour, black letter), the route number 34px in its bus colour (trunk #3c88ee, branch #2aaf55, express #c8302f), crowding at the right (Crowded in #ff6b6b, the others #b5b5b5), the action 21px in amber #ffb020 (Add 2 buses · Re-space; On plan in white), a bar of the longest gap with a white tick at the planned gap, the stop and its number. Then up to eight rows (type, number, action, bar, minutes); the rest on one line ('+ 5 more routes, all on plan'). Rows in two columns when the board is 620px or wider. Order: add buses, re-space, then on plan, each by how far the longest gap runs past the plan

sample.topic: Weekly service report of Vizney Transit, a fictional city's subway (Lines 1, 2 and 3, 38 stations) and its feeder buses (15 routes), week 48 (Nov 23–29, 2026) against week 47 and the plan: boardings, on-time trips, the 8–9 am load of every segment in both directions with its busiest 15 minutes and the trips needed for 150%, bus passing times at the station stops (7–9 am, Monday to Friday) with the headway kept and the longest gap, gate entries by hour at the stations, and delays of 5 minutes or more. Every station name, station number, route number and figure is invented. The bus routes use zone 8, which Seoul's numbering (zones 0–7) does not have

canvas.role: page, cards and plots: seoul.go.kr's white

line.role: 1px card outlines and the rule under the header: seoul.go.kr's line

hair.role: table row rules, the bus strips' baselines, 30-minute grid in Figure 4

rule.role: 1.5px rule under table heads and over the total row

ink.role: titles, values, the selected filter pill (white text 17.2:1), transfer capsule edges, gate-staff outlines

body.role: body text: seoul.go.kr's most used text colour (15.9:1)

text-2.role: labels, table heads, keys, station numbers (5.4:1): seoul.go.kr's second text colour

dark.role: the all-lines band on the station signs, bus dots in Figure 4, the cause the title names in Table 1, step numbers: seoul.go.kr's dark surface

pill.role: the EN/KO switch and the compare switch: seoul.go.kr's grey surface

side.role: the package list and the code pane in the build bench

tag.role: the 150% tag and the tags on segments over 150% (ink text 11.9:1): Seoul Metro's crowding chart

limit.role: the dashed 150% line in Figure 3: Seoul Metro's crowding chart

board.role: the bus information terminal; the only black on the page

board-line.role: tile edges and row rules on the board

amber.role: action words on the board and the bars of routes that need action (10.6:1): the BIT's 'arriving soon' words

lines.role: the line colours, moved from Seoul's official values into the lightness band and apart for colour-blind readers. A line is always named by its number circle (the text step with a white number: #2160b0 6.2:1, #0a7a3c 5.4:1, #b34900 5.4:1), its name and its place on the map, never by colour alone

bus.role: Seoul's bus colours by route type, on the board only; every route number carries its type letter (B · G · R; black on blue 5.5:1 and green 6.8:1, white on red 5.4:1). Route numbers are large text, 34px in the tiles and 19px/700 in the rows, so the express red (3.6:1) clears 3:1. On white (route boxes in Figure 4) the darker steps with white numbers

crowding.role: the city's crowding scale; on the map as line widths, in text as the words. Bus crowding on the board: Seats · Normal · Crowded (여유 · 보통 · 혼잡)

status.role: a good change is blue, a bad one red, always with ▲ ▼ and words. Red never shares a figure with Line 3's orange (normal-vision ΔE 8.2): the map and the single-line diagram have no red

heat.role: Figure 5: gate entries an hour, under 500 in #f1f0f6, then the five purples; 4,000 and over (gate staff) gets a 2px ink outline and, where the cell is 34px or wider, the value in white

text.role: values and labels stay in ink; changes blue when good and red when bad

validation.lines: #2160b0 · #1aac52 · #c45000 on #ffffff, light, all pairs: all checks pass; worst CVD ΔE 8.0 (deutan, orange and green) at the floor, so a line always carries its number circle, name and position; normal-vision ΔE 27.9; green 2.97:1 on white, relieved by labels. Grey #9a9a9a (other operators) and #b3b7bd (under 150%) are grey on purpose: normal-vision ΔE 17.6 and 21.6 or more from the lines
validation.bus: #3c88ee · #2aaf55 · #c8302f on #0d0d0d, dark, all pairs: all checks pass, worst CVD ΔE 10.3, normal 27.8, all 3:1 or more
validation.sequential: #b9a9ea · #9a83dc · #7c5fca · #5f42ab · #432a85 --ordinal: one hue (5°), monotone, every step ΔL ≥ 0.06, light end 2.12:1 on white
validation.diverging: arms checked apart --ordinal: #8fb2ea · #4f86d6 · #1f5aa8 (3°) and #efa09b · #de5a55 · #b3192b (2°) pass; midpoint #d9d9d9
validation.status: #1f5aa8 · #c8102e · #b3b7bd, all pairs: the two colours separate; grey is grey on purpose (1.96:1, always with a value)
validation.text: on white: ink 17.2, body 15.9, muted #616b7e 5.4, blue #1f5aa8 6.8, red #c8102e 5.9, line text steps 6.2 · 5.4 · 5.4; ink on #ffd23f 11.9; on the board: white 19.4, #b5b5b5 9.5, amber 10.6, #ff6b6b 7.0

code.note: the line text steps and two status colours; every token 4.5:1 or more on #f7f8fa

sans.role: every word and number, one body face per language: seoul.go.kr sets Korean in Pretendard Variable (16px body) and english.seoul.go.kr sets English in Noto Sans. Numbers tabular

typography.city-fonts: Seoul's own typefaces (Seoul Hangang, Seoul Namsan, Seoul Alrim) are free for anyone to use but may not be sold or redistributed, so the sample and the package do not load them as web fonts. A company that installs them on its own machines can set them in Tableau and Power BI

scale.headline: 26px/700 (ko 25px), line-height 1.3; 21px under 640px
scale.card-title: 19px/700 (ko 18.5px), the figure number above it 12.5px/700 muted
scale.kpi: label 14.5px/700; value 38px/700 tabular in the pill (32px under 330px, 26px under 262px), unit 18px/700; band sides 14.5px/700 with an 11.5px word under; the change 13.5px
scale.map: station names 12px/600 (700 at the ends of segments over 150%) with a 3px white halo; tags 11.5px/700
scale.single-line: names 12.5px (700 for the run over 150%), station numbers 10.5px muted tabular, values 12.5px/700, direction heads 12.5px/700, the tag 11px/700
scale.board: route numbers 34px/700 in tiles and 19px/700 in rows, actions 21px/700 in tiles, rows 14px, small text 12–12.5px
scale.table: minutes 15px/700, station number 12px muted before the name, cause 14px (700 for the cause the title names)

typography.notation: boardings in K and M (821K, 4.16M) and in 만 in Korean (82.1만, 416만); percent with one decimal for rates (97.9%), whole for crowding (168%); points as pts (ko %p); minutes as 13 min (13분); times 24-hour 08:12; station numbers three digits before the name (264 Maehwa-dong); route numbers as they are (810, 8827); directions as Seoul names them: inner loop · outer loop (내선순환 · 외선순환) on Line 2, toward the end station (너른들 방면) on the others; ▲ ▼ before every change; real minus −

rows: header 60px, white with a 1px #dedede rule: Vizney Transit and the report name, the EN/KO switch
Week 48 · Nov 23–29, 2026 · against week 47 and the plan, with the line filter on the right (All lines · ① Line 1 · ② Line 2 · ③ Line 3, pills with number circles)
KPI row: four station signs (boardings, on-time trips, peak crowding, bus gaps kept)
first screen (1440×810): Figure 1, the line map | Figure 2, the bus board (520px). Bottoms on one line
Lines and buses: Figure 3, the single-line diagram | Figure 4, buses passing the stops
Stations and delays: Figure 5, station × hour | Table 1, delays of 5 minutes or more (eight rows and the rest on demand, a total row)

layout.responsive: 1360 and over: the board 520px; 1200–1359: 480px. Under 1200: Figures 1 and 2 and the stations row stack across the page; the map takes the height of its own shape and the board's rows run in two columns. Under 1024: KPI 2×2 and Figures 3 and 4 stack. Under 900: Table 1 drops trains held. Under 640: one column, the line filter in four equal pills, the sign values under the band, the table drops the time and the bars

motion.lines: the map's lines fade in by line, 140ms apart
motion.bars: 0.45s, Figure 3's bars grow out from the strip, 26ms a row; values fade in after
motion.board: the action words light up in three steps, 140ms apart
motion.fade: 0.3s for the bus strips and the heat cells

tableau.fonts: Tableau Book for text; Noto Sans or Pretendard only if installed on every viewing machine and the server

measured.seoul.go.kr: Pretendard Variable, body 16px; text #222222 (most used), second #616b7e, also #333 and #555; dark surface #363743; surfaces #ffffff · #eeeeee · #fafafa; lines 1px #dedede · #e1e3e8; accents orange-red #ff553c · #ff5034 and blue #0065ee; sizes 40/700, 32/700, 24/700, 20/600, 18/400, 16/400; corners 20px (most used), 30px, 40px, 10px, pills and circles 50%
measured.line-colours: Seoul's line colour sheet (May 2025, the new map): 1 #004A85, 2 #00A23F, 3 #ED6C00, 4 #009BCE, 5 #794698, 6 #7C4932, 7 #6E7E31, 8 #D11D70, 9 #A49D87. Badges are line-colour circles with a white number

notice.en: Not an official design of the Seoul Metropolitan Government or Seoul Metro, and not affiliated with or endorsed by them. A reference style read from the publicly visible design of seoul.go.kr and public touchpoints such as subway station signs, the subway map and bus information terminals; it carries no logo, typeface, photo or data of theirs. Trademarks belong to their owners.

notice.why: No naming guideline or set notice was found for describing the city by name. The city emblem, logos, slogan and mascot, Seoul Metro's logo and character, the map artwork and landmark pictograms (KOGL type 4: no commercial use, no changes), real station names, numbers, routes, bus numbers and stop numbers, and photos are not used
